correctness.rationale: Canonical rotation by anchoring 1 and unique reversal orientation a2<a_n gives a bijection to dihedral classes. Every permutation branch occurs exactly once in the exhaustive recursion. Multiply all possible reciprocal denominators by LCM(3,...,2n-1) and perform exact uint64 integer equality. Maximum sum nL/3<2^64 for n<=13; no overflow, signed rounding or numerical tolerance. Actual packaged verifier ran all sizes and asserted values. A second independent exact Fraction enumeration checked both n8 representatives and n9=5. No infinite claim.

value.rationale: The newly resolved existential problem naturally asks whether its solutions are unique, rare, or abundant. The first feasible circular n=8 has exactly TWO distinct classes, and the complete successive orbit multiplicities through n=13 provide the first rigorously bounded natural initial spectrum, including the first substantial growth to 38 at n=11. Exact finite counts give reproducible benchmark data for orbit-counting methods and constructions. The already published linear spectrum was intentionally excluded. This is not a claim of a general asymptotic theorem.
